svg.title: TOPAK D9 — The archive of record: what the log ordered, what a round sealed, what a build pinned, kept in two stores and an index, on one retention schedule
svg.desc: ADR-0074 says what the archive holds and how it is fed: five holdings, each a copy from one source by a program that only reads, and a segment of the log is held before a mark the log orders says so. ADR-0075 gives every holding a line in one retention schedule: facts are never erased, a round unit ends by erasure or by period and is dropped whole, every absence is explained by a fact, and a hold may only preserve. ADR-0076 makes the archive a locked store, a governed store and an index, with the log ordering the root of every segment and nothing that decides reading the archive without a proof. All three are Proposed (2026.11.16), unreviewed, and nothing in them is modelled, checked or built: ADR-0005 §5 still holds, "The archive does not exist at the reference". D3 draws the four record planes; this diagram opens the archive plane and does not redraw D3.
svg.text: TOPAK · D9

text.tspan: The archive of record: what the log ordered, what a round sealed, what a build pinned, kept in two stores and an index, on one retention schedule

svg.text: ADR-0074 says what the archive holds and how it is fed: five holdings, each a copy from one source by a program that only reads, and a segment of the log is held before a mark the log orders says so. ADR-0075 gives every holding a line in one retention schedule: facts are never erased, a round unit ends by erasure or by period and is dropped whole, every absence is explained by a fact, and a hold may only preserve. ADR-0076 makes the archive a locked store, a governed store and an

index, with the log ordering the root of every segment and nothing that decides reading the archive without a proof. All three are Proposed (2026.11.16), unreviewed, and nothing in them is modelled, checked or built: ADR-0005 §5 still holds, "The archive does not exist at the reference". D3 draws the four record planes; this diagram opens the archive plane and does not redraw D3.

text.tspan: the mechanism record for the mark and compaction
the dependent entries (ADR-0075 Annex B; ADR-0076 Annex B)
floor entries: the hold, the readers' proviso
the stores, the index, their products
Proposed · on another branch, not here
a reader who is not the drafter

svg.text: Proposed means nothing here is in force. The custodian's request of 2026.11.16 settled three things the set uses: ⟨K10⟩ every revision and every checkpoint or release of the documentation stays reachable, equal to the latest; ⟨K11⟩ a separate set of records for the archive of record; ⟨K12⟩ the set conforms to TOPAK's retention requirements, follows good practice and is informed by the documentation's design. ADR-0076 also applies ⟨K5⟩ (a single-table store behind the DynamoDB interface) and ⟨K6⟩ (GraphQL and REST), said of the

documentation, on the strength of ⟨K12⟩. Every other choice is the drafter's, marked (drafter's choice) or (drafter's recommendation) in the records and kept so here. One author, one day; ADR-0075 R2 the same day, after reading ADR-0070. The three records cite each other and ask to be ratified together.

text.tspan: The archive plane opened: four sources, two stores, an index, the mark, and who reads (ADR-0074 §1–§4; ADR-0076 §1, §6, §7)
the archive · the system of record (ADR-0005 §1) · not built (ADR-0005 §5; G9)
the sources: each holding has one (ADR-0074 §2 H-2)
Built at reference · 3 replicas; nothing compacted (G14)

svg.text: The ordering authority (ADR-0015; D3). Every entry of every kind is a fact for holding A, read in
index order (ADR-0074 §2, §3 F-1).
Orders the archive mark for a held segment, on its own recomputation of the root (ADR-0074 §4
A-2, A-4): the roots are facts, and an auditor has them from the log (ADR-0076 §5 IN-2).
Discards no entry above the newest mark (ADR-0074 §4 A-3). An unmarked log grows and
never loses an entry (A-5).
The F6 entry is how an erasure reaches the archive, and by no other path (ADR-0075 §3 ER-1).
The corpus is a holding (drafter's choice: no record says the corpus is archived). A cut is the files
one manifest measures (ADR-0074 §2 C, H-6).
The feeder is given a manifest and a commit, refuses a tree that does not verify, and stores each
file under its digest, once (§3 F-6).
Trust is T-0045-11's and no better: one person cuts the manifests (§7).

text.tspan: Where a citing fact's author put it

svg.text: Evidence: an object a fact cites by digest that is neither payload nor corpus: attestation evidence,
gate evidence, promoted artifacts and signatures, the genesis bundle, issued rules (§2 D).
When a segment is ingested each cited digest is looked for; a digest with no object is recorded
as *missing* and never passed over in silence (§3 F-7).
Transport, not the record (ADR-0005 §1; D3). A sealed round topic with its after companion is
holding B's unit (ADR-0074 §2 B).
Captured after the seal, whole, judged by nothing: no filter, redaction or summary (§3 F-2, F-9).
Masking is the write path's, before the seal.
Capture does not touch the topic: it is dropped on its own schedule; a topic that expires
uncaptured is lost to the archive and its header says not captured (F-4; ADR-0003 A3).
At the archetype every unit is captured (drafter's choice) (F-5).
Holds A facts as segments, C the corpus, D evidence, E the journal (§1). Duty: keep, unchanged, for each line's at
least. Failure: evidence lost or damaged.
LS-1 Every object under the SHA-256 of its bytes, written once. LS-2 Under a lock no credential can shorten or lift
(compliance mode or a declared equivalent), extended before it ends, never shortened; a lock that lapses under its line
is a finding. LS-3 In every declared fault domain: at least three, under two administrations, one sharing no site with the
replicas (drafter's choice). LS-4 Bytes as written; a segment names the cut whose formats it uses. LS-5 Ceph's object
gateway (drafter's recommendation).
A segment is *held* when its bytes are in this store in every declared fault domain and each copy hashes to its root
A facts: every log entry, in segments, complete and gapless (§3 F-1) · C cuts, by manifest · D objects, by digest · E the
journal: ingests, marks received, fixity results, drops, reads; the one thing the archive originates (§1 K-4), with a tree of
its own whose root each mark carries (ADR-0076 §5 IN-6).

text.tspan: The governed store (ADR-0076 §3) · D3's plaintext store · T-0045-40, proposed

svg.text: Holds B round units and nothing else: ADR-0004's store "built for deletion". Duty: keep until erasure or period, and
then no longer. Failure: a unit lost early; a unit not deleted.
GS-1 One container, one store, for the unit's whole time: no tiering. GS-2 No version, no lock; a deleted object is gone
from every read at once. GS-3 Dropped when no read in any domain returns it, purged when the bytes leave the media;
the deployment declares the purge interval. GS-4 Nothing derived from a unit outside it. GS-5 Held in the domains
declared for payload, each receiving every drop. GS-6 The same gateway, separately deployed, versioning off (drafter's
recommendation).
Shares nothing with the locked store: no bucket, volume, credential or administrator's role (§1 P-1). The only right to
delete is the executor's, on an F6 entry or the end of a period.
One table behind the DynamoDB interface, under ADR-0072 §5's contract ⟨K5⟩: composite key, every access a key
condition, none a scan, immutability by conditional write (IX-1; Annex A).
A projection of both stores: fields of facts, unit headers, cut manifests (§1). It is not the record: dropped and rebuilt, the
rebuild checked against the roots (P-2, IX-3).
No attribute derived from a body (IX-2; ADR-0075 §3 ER-5). A unit's item says it exists, where, its digest and its state,
not what is in it.
Engine: ExtendDB on PostgreSQL (drafter's recommendation), new and self-declared for development; tolerable here
and not for either store (IX-4).
Every read is by an identified reader under a reader set, declared per holding and, for A, per forensic class (RD-1).
Reader sets are policy in a promoted bundle (drafter's choice); the audit authority is never removed (RD-2; ADR-0028
GraphQL and REST, generated from one model, equal, read-only (RD-3; ADR-0072 §7). Every past state is read as
the newest (RD-5).
An answer about a fact carries its inclusion proof and names its mark (RD-7): the service and the index are
conveniences the reader need not trust.
Every read but a read of C is entered in the journal (RD-6), with the reader, the set, the ask and a stated purpose
nothing checks. A read writes nothing else (RD-8).
Export: any readable range as one self-describing package (a BagIt bag, RFC 8493, drafter's choice) that verifies with no
access to the archive (EX-1, EX-2). A package of units is a copy no erasure reaches (EX-3).
"the anchor plus a declared external auditor role" (ADR-0028 §3); the role is undefined (ADR-0076 §11; ADR-0028, Open
obligations). Reads A always, every class, and E.
Read B: whoever the topic's ACL named (ADR-0003 0003.3), carried to the unit (drafter's choice), and the "Separate read-only
principals for audit". Readers of D: as the fact that cites the object.
Reads C, which is published; a deployment's own cuts as it declares. The documentation service (ADR-0072 §1 P-1, Proposed)
reads holding C and nothing else, and its store can be rebuilt from C (ADR-0074 §5 C-4).

text.tspan: A gate, a tally, a tool that needs a compacted entry

svg.text: Takes it only with an inclusion proof against a mark in the log (AR-2); an entry without one is absent and the gate fails. Absence
only subtracts (AR-3). Lineage (ADR-0035 §1) and the intake gate that reruns an extractor (ADR-0069 §3a IG-4), both Proposed, are
the first two readers this binds.

text.tspan: The admit path, and anything that decides on a unit

svg.text: The admit path does not read the archive (AR-1): true of the reference today, and kept true. Nothing decides on a unit (AR-4): no
admit, gate or tally reads holding B. So an archive that fails in any way, lying included, produces no admit, promotion or issuance the
mechanism would otherwise refuse (§6).
① segments, in index order
③ a cut, by manifest
④ objects, by digest
② a sealed unit, whole
⑤ the mark: the archive reports a root, a replica recomputes it, the log orders it
⑥ an F6 entry: drop the unit whole
⑦ fields; manifests
⑦ the unit's header
answers
a unit's records
⑧ reads
no read
P · the log
K · transport
the locked store
the governed store (D3's plaintext store); readers
the index: a projection
the read service
a feeder or a read: not built
erasure; a path denied
The arrows (every one is a path nothing has built)

The facts feeder reads the log in index order and writes segments: complete, in order, no gap between one and the segment before (ADR-0074 §3 F-1). A feeder is a program in the repository, named by digest, that reads one source and writes one holding, holds no credential that could write to a source, and judges nothing (§1 K-3; §3 F-9). Ingest is idempotent and addressed by content (F-8).

The round-unit feeder reads a topic after its seal (Run: ADR-0042 §5; Build: the topic set, ADR-0021 §3) and writes the unit as one container, with the after companion as its second member (F-2). The header is a fact and the container is payload (F-3).

The corpus feeder is given a manifest and a commit, refuses a tree that does not verify, and stores each file under its digest with the manifest as the cut's index (F-6). Reads what ADR-0029's genesis bundle and corpus manifest format define, which is open.
Evidence is looked for by each digest a segment's facts cite; found, it is written under its digest; a digest with no object is recorded as missing (F-7).

The archive mark (drafter's choice): an entry the mechanism orders for a held segment, naming its range and its root; not an admit, promotion or issuance, and it enables nothing (§4 A-2). A replica proposes it only for a root it recomputed from its own log; a wrong root is refused (A-4). Kinds: held (this record's), erased and disposed (ADR-0075's), the last two recording the archive's report, which A-4 cannot reach (A-7). The marks are facts, in the next segment (A-6). Each mark also carries the journal's root, which the mechanism cannot recompute (ADR-0076 §5

Erasure reaches the archive as the F6 fact and by no other path (ADR-0075 §3 ER-1): the feeder of facts sees the entry, the entry names units, the governed store drops each container whole in every fault domain. When every copy is gone the archive reports it and the mechanism orders the erased mark; between the two the erasure is ordered and not complete, and that state is listable (ER-2). Disposition at the end of a period takes the same path with a disposed mark (§5 DP-1, DP-2).

The index is a projection of both stores: fields of facts and of headers, cut manifests, and no attribute derived from a body (ADR-0076 §1, §4 IX-2). Dropped, it is rebuilt from the stores and checked against the roots (P-2).

A read is by an identified reader under a reader set (RD-1), answered through GraphQL or REST (RD-3), with the inclusion proof and the mark for any fact (RD-7), and journalled unless it reads C (RD-6). The admit path never reads the archive (§6 AR-1), and no admit, gate or tally reads a unit (AR-4).

text.tspan: ADR-0074 · The archive keeps what the log ordered, what a round sealed, what a fact cites and what a manifest measured, and originates none of it
Proposed · C2, C4 · R1 · drafted 2026.11.16, not reviewed

svg.text: Context. The corpus says where the record is kept and nothing about the place: ADR-0005 §1 names the archive as the system of record, ADR-0004 keeps the hash and a pointer in the record and plaintext in a store built for deletion, ADR-0003 A3 makes the archive "a separate store fed by that ETL and ... not a tier of the topic", T-0045-7 trusts it to retain what was written, and ADR-0005 §5 says it does not exist at the reference. No record says what the ETL takes, when, or on whose word. ADR-0005 and ADR-0024 §8 give two right

answers to which store is the record: the archive keeps, the log authors. The corpus keeps itself in a repository on a carrier whose identifiers "locate and do not identify" (ADR-0069 §9 C-5, Proposed), and ⟨K10⟩ asks that every revision stay reachable. Status note: C2 (§2's exhaustiveness and §1's confinement) and C4 attach; C1 is ADR-0075's; C3: nothing accepted is reversed, and §4 A-3 adds a precondition to a compaction no record has decided. Deployment position: Archetype.

text.tspan: §1 The archive keeps and never originates ⟨K11⟩ · §2 Five holdings ⟨K12⟩, the table whole
K-1 Every item is a copy

svg.text: Of an entry the log ordered, a round topic the mechanism sealed, an object a fact cites by digest, or a file a manifest measured;
each carries what says which: a log index, a round's identity and seal, a digest, a manifest line.

text.tspan: K-2 The log says what happened; the archive is where that is kept

svg.text: A fact is in the archive because it was in the log. Where a copy and the log disagree, the log is right and the copy is a
finding. When the log no longer holds an entry (§4), the copy stands on the mark that covers it and on nothing else.

text.tspan: K-3 No program in the archive writes to a source

svg.text: The feeders read the log, the transport and the repository, and hold no credential that could write to any of them.

text.tspan: K-4 The one exception: the archive's account of itself

svg.text: What it ingested, checked, dropped and showed to whom (holding E). A record about the archive, not a fact about any principal's
action; nothing reads it to decide anything.
This keeps T-0045-7's class: a store that only copies can lose a copy, which is "legibility subtracted, authority untouched".
ADR-0076 §6 closes the remaining route.
Facts: every entry of the consensus log, whatever its kind. Admits (F1), stop attributions (F2), votes (F3), issuances (F4), break-glass
invocations (F5), erasure events (F6), and every other entry: lease and epoch transitions, seals, and the marks of §4
The log
A segment: a contiguous range of log indices
No
Round units: a sealed round topic with its after companion, whole. Envelopes, denials and bodies together: raw emissions, Actuate
records, the task, the tool list, review commentary
The transport, after the seal
A unit: one principal's round in one rules-epoch
chain
Yes, whole
The corpus: records, checkpoints, manifests, modules and results, the floor, the narrative and its revisions, derived documents,
documentation releases (ADR-0071 §8), and the reference trees
The repository, at a manifest
A cut: the files one manifest measures
No
ADR-0029 §5; T-0045-11; the checkpoints' convention G-C1
Evidence: an object a fact cites by digest that is neither payload nor corpus. Attestation evidence, gate-evidence files, promoted
artifacts and their signatures, the genesis bundle, issued rules, the review attestation; lineage records and corpus-root manifests if
ADR-0035 and ADR-0069 are ratified
Where the citing fact's author put it
An object, by digest
No, unless it embeds payload, when it is in B
The archive's journal: ingests, marks received, fixity results, drops, and reads
The archive
An entry
No

text.tspan: H-1 The list is exhaustive · H-2 One source, one feeder

svg.text: A thing a record says is retained, kept or archived belongs to one holding; a record that adds such a thing names its holding or
adds one here. Each holding has one source and one feeder (§3).

text.tspan: H-3 Payload is only ever in B · H-4 A denial is in B

svg.text: A, C, D and E hold no cognitive payload (ADR-0004); evidence that carries payload goes in its unit so an erasure reaches it.
A denial is a control-plane fact and not in the log (ADR-0005 §2: "by the deciding replica, unordered"); it is kept and dropped with
its round.

text.tspan: H-5 Three things are not holdings

svg.text: The correlator's store, "a cache and never a source" (ADR-0051 §6, Proposed).
A replica's security log of attempts with no session, which no record places.
The live content store behind a corpus root (ADR-0069 §10.1, Proposed): Build's working store. The root's promoted manifests
are in D.

text.tspan: H-6 The corpus is a holding (drafter's choice)

svg.text: No record says the corpus is archived. A deployment's archive holds the cuts its genesis bundle and promotions cite. During
genesis there is no deployment, and §7 says what holding C is then.

text.tspan: §4 A segment is held before a mark says so · §5 What the archive keeps for the documentation ⟨K10⟩ ⟨K12⟩ · §7 During genesis · §8 The trusted base

svg.text: A-1 Held: bytes in the locked store in every declared fault domain, each copy hashing to the root.
A-2 The mechanism orders an archive mark naming range and root (drafter's choice). ADR-0063 (Proposed) orders a watermark
the same way and owes "a record that goes up in segments with a receipt": the mark is that receipt.
A-3 No replica discards an entry above the newest mark (drafter's choice). ADR-0045 §6 leaves compaction inside the verified
object and no record decides when it may run.
A-4 Checked, not believed: proposed only for a root the replica recomputed; a wrong root is refused.
A-5 An unmarked log grows: storage and, at the limit, availability; never an entry.
A-6 The marks are facts, in holding A, in the next segment.
A-7 Kinds: held here; erased and disposed are ADR-0075's and record the archive's report, which A-4 cannot reach. A false one
is T-0045-7's residual with a mark that claims otherwise; ADR-0076 §5's audit looks for it.
C-1 Every cut is kept whole and verifies as cut: a manifest is checked "against the tree it measured, not against today's" (
manifests/README.md), with no carrier.
C-2 Every revision of a file is reachable: by digest, by path in a cut, and across cuts as the sequence of digests one path has had.
C-3 A cut is never preferred for being newer; which checkpoint is the state of record is the corpus's statement (
checkpoints/README.md), kept in the cut that makes it.
C-4 The documentation service reads holding C and nothing else (ADR-0072 §1 P-1). Its store can be rebuilt from C; C is rebuilt
from nothing.
C-5 What a manifest excludes is not kept by it: manifests/EXCLUDE leaves the two guides, the diagrams and the READMEs
unmeasured; a documentation release (ADR-0071 §8) measures the unit files.
No log, no round, no deployment: holdings A, B and D are empty at every site but the reference's tests.
Holding C can exist now: an archive of the corpus's cuts, fed by manifest, under the custodian's custody (1, 0). It would make
G1 to G11 readable as cut without a carrier and be the first thing the documentation service projects.
Its trust is T-0045-11's and no better: one person cuts the manifests it is fed.
Not built. The record names G1 to G11; G12 was cut 2026.11.16, the same day.
Which units are captured is declared per use case (ADR-0003 0003.4); at the archetype every unit (drafter's choice: ADR-0028's
"maximum projection"; ADR-0037 §3 retains raw emission). Running a feeder twice writes nothing the second time.

text.tspan: §8 The trusted base: T-0045-7 stays delegated

svg.text: Three things are new and none is a row: the feeders read and copy, and A-4 and F-7 make a failure visible; the mark is ordered
by the mechanism on its own recomputation, so the archive's word is not taken; holding C's feeder stands behind T-0045-11 and
adds nothing.
ADR-0076 Annex B proposes that T-0045-7 become two rows, since the archive and the plaintext store have opposite duties.
On ratification and building the set would discharge ADR-0034's debt against "archive and plaintext store (evidence retention,
§3)", give T-0045-7 the content ADR-0045 lists it as lacking, and answer part of ADR-0029's open item on the corpus manifest.

text.tspan: Nothing here is modelled, checked or built.
§6 The archive in OAIS's terms (ISO 14721:2025; informative, no conformance claimed) · §9 Degeneracy on this record

svg.text: The log, the transport, the repository. Never a person
A range of log entries, a sealed topic, a tree at a manifest, an object by digest
The feeders (§3) and the mark (§4)
A segment with its root; a unit with its header; a cut with its manifest; an object with its digest

text.tspan: Preservation description: provenance, fixity, reference, context,

svg.text: The source position (§1 K-1); digests and roots (ADR-0076 §5); ids; chain, epoch, round and fence; reader sets (ADR-0076 §7)
The schedule (ADR-0075 §1); fixity and format (ADR-0076 §5)
The read interfaces and the export (ADR-0076 §7, §8)
The audit authority (ADR-0028 §3), and the readers ADR-0071 §2 lists
Capture → partial
Some use cases' units are not captured
None. No theorem reads a unit
After a topic's own retention ends, nothing holds its payload. ADR-0037's D-0037-2 is the instance for raw emission
Mark → absent
Segments are archived and no mark is ordered
§4 A-3, and every property of ADR-0076 §5 that reads a
mark
A compacted log's entries stand on the archive's word alone, or the log is never compacted. This is the reference's position, with nothing
compacted
Corpus → not held
Holding C is omitted
None
The corpus is where a carrier has it. ADR-0072's service projects a repository, not a record. This is today's position

text.tspan: §10 Ratification condition, item by item (every item Not met, as the record marks it)
State, as the record marks it

svg.text: A module states §1 and §4 and its mutations break them (ADR-0046's method). At least ArchiveOriginatesNothing (M_FEEDERWRITES), MarkedOnlyIfHeld (M_EARLYMARK), NoDiscardAboveMark (M_COMPACTEARLY), MissingIsRecorded (M_SILENTSKIP)
Not met. No module is written
A mechanism record decides the archive mark and the compaction rule (A-2, A-3)
Not met. None is drafted

The reference shows: a segment ingested, held and marked; a mark refused for a wrong root; a round unit captured after its seal with its after member; a cut ingested by manifest and one refused for a tree that does not verify; a cited digest recorded as missing
Not met. Nothing is built
Holding C exists for G1 to G11 (§7), or the custodian decides it waits

text.tspan: The dependent entries of ADR-0076 Annex B are drafted

svg.text: Not met. None is drafted

text.tspan: ADR-0075 and ADR-0076 are ratified, or this record is ratified with them

svg.text: Not met. Both are Proposed
A reader who is not the drafter (ADR-0029 A2)
The custodian's reading of every drafter's choice and recommendation, the corpus as a holding and the mark among them

text.tspan: Options considered, whole · Consequences · Open obligations · History
One record for the whole archive

svg.text: Not taken ⟨K11⟩. The request asks for a set. Holdings, lifetime and storage change for different reasons, which is ADR-0003's own lesson: four of its seven clauses turned out to be separately supersedable

text.tspan: The log as the system of record, kept for ever, and no archive

svg.text: Rejected. ADR-0005 §1 is accepted and names the archive. A log that is never compacted is the reference's position and "Fine for a baseline, not for a service" (mechanism/ G14)

text.tspan: The transport as the record, with long retention

svg.text: Rejected by ADR-0005 §1, which names the transport as "Not the holder"

text.tspan: The archive as a tier of the topic

svg.text: Rejected by ADR-0003 A3

text.tspan: An archive that accepts writes from principals or operators: notes, annotations, corrections

svg.text: Rejected (§1). It would originate. A correction to the record is a new fact in the log

text.tspan: Facts and units in one holding

svg.text: Rejected. ADR-0004 separates them so that one can be destroyed and the other cannot

text.tspan: The mark as the archive's signed receipt, under an archive key

svg.text: Not taken (drafter's choice). The key would be a trust root for whether evidence exists, with its own issuance and custody. A-4 has the mechanism recompute, and needs no key

text.tspan: No compaction rule here, leaving A-3 to a mechanism record

svg.text: Open. A-3 is stated here because the archive is not the record without it. The custodian may prefer it in the record that owns the log

text.tspan: The corpus not a holding, left to the repository

svg.text: Open (D-0074-3). It is today's position. It leaves ⟨K10⟩ resting on a carrier

Not taken. They are not in the log, and ordering them there "contradicts ADR-0015" (ADR-0003, A2 note). Whether a denial should outlive its round is a question for ADR-0003 and ADR-0020 and is not moved here

text.tspan: Capture decided by the feeder: sampling, or keeping only rounds with findings

svg.text: Rejected (F-9). It would make a judgment about content decide what evidence exists

text.tspan: The correlator's store as a holding

svg.text: Not taken (H-5). ADR-0051 is Proposed and makes it a cache

Positive: the store five records lean on has a description; "the record" has one meaning; the log can be compacted without losing the record and not before it is safe; the archive cannot be made to say
something happened; the corpus has a home that is not a carrier; a missing piece of evidence is a recorded fact.

Negative: the mechanism gains a log entry and a constraint on compaction with no module or record; replicas' storage is coupled to the archive's health (A-5); capturing every unit is large; a captured unit is a
second copy of erasable data; holding C duplicates a repository during genesis; denials die with their round, and ADR-0020 calls them "the only evidence containment did anything".
The mechanism record for the mark and compaction, with its module.
A sequence number on denials (ADR-0005 §6; G9 item 44).
The replica security log, which no record places (H-5).
Whether a denial should survive its round's erasure, as a fact with no payload.
Segment size and cadence: A-5's storage cost against the feeder's lag.
The genesis bundle and corpus manifest format (ADR-0029), which F-6 reads.
The overlay's plane records (ADR-0062, ADR-0063; Proposed), which arrive already in segments.
Narrative: ToO §4 and the glossary owe holding, segment, unit, cut, feeder and archive mark if ratified.
— Initial draft, 2026.11.16, by the assistant at the custodian's direction, not reviewed.

R1 Revision before ratification: renumbered from ADR-0073 to ADR-0074 with its five siblings, each up by one, because ADR-0070 was taken by a record in flight on another branch (pull request #51) that the
first draft's check of fetched branches missed. No decision text changes. Not reviewed.

text.tspan: ADR-0075 · Every holding has a line in one retention schedule; facts are never erased; a round unit is dropped whole; every absence is explained by a fact; a hold may only preserve; a closed chain's record is still kept
Proposed · C1, C2, C4 · R2 · drafted 2026.11.16, not reviewed

svg.text: Context. The retention rules exist clause by clause in a dozen records and have never been in one table: F1 to F6 "non-erasable for the declared horizon", the chain's lifetime at the archetype (ADR-0028 §1, §3); Run's topics "per use case" (ADR-0003 0003.4); Build's "for the production lifetime of any artifact promoted from that round" (ADR-0021 §7); raw emission the same (ADR-0037 §3); no length for anything else. The records disagree at the edges: T-0045-7 covers "The archive and plaintext store" with one identity, "object lock or

equivalent", while ADR-0004 wants plaintext "built for deletion"; ADR-0003's Context has both "nothing ever be removed" and erasure "provably"; ADR-0006 records an erasure "in the log it modifies" while ADR-0003 says hash chains are never edited; ADR-0028's horizon "does not survive re-genesis" and lists HIPAA's six years as unresolved; CR-11 notes that who exercised authority is personal data. No record fixes a retention length in any unit of time, and this one fixes none. Status note: C1 (§3, §4 put a proof obligation on

erasure), C2 (§1, §4), C4 (ADR-0006's required property stated; ADR-0038 finding 3; ADR-0028's re-genesis obligation in part); C3: §2's line for facts outside F1 to F6 extends ADR-0028's horizon, and a reviewer may read that as more than a restatement. R2 reconciles the record with ADR-0070 (Proposed, on another branch) ⟨K13⟩: §8a, HD-3 and DP-4 revised; SC-5, AS-6, AS-7, ER-8 and D-0075-4 new. Erasure is not implemented and no erasure roster exists (G11).

text.tspan: §1 One schedule, a line for every holding ⟨K12⟩: the six fields · §2 The archetype's schedule, whole

svg.text: A holding of ADR-0074 §2, or a named part of one
The event that begins the period. Always a fact in the log or a seal. Never a date someone enters
What the class is kept for whatever anyone asks. Shortening it is the change the line's last field names
When the class must be gone, if a limit applies. Empty for a class that is kept without limit
never, erasure (§3), period (§5), or both
What it takes to shorten at least: a floor relaxation, a declaration, or nothing
SC-1 A period is counted from a fact, in the deployment's clock model (ADR-0032). Where no record supplies a value the line reads "the deployment writes this", and a
schedule with such a line unfilled is incomplete.
SC-2 At least protects evidence; at most limits exposure. A line may carry both.
SC-3 Lengthening at least is always allowed: ADR-0028's "more, never less".
SC-4 The schedule is promoted with the declaration; each line states its basis *(drafter's choice; CR-11 asks for "a legal-basis line per class")*.
SC-5 ⟨R2⟩ A line may say where its class may be held: ADR-0070's B25 practice, "Residency declared per data class". This record does not become B25's owner.

text.tspan: AS-1 Every log entry is kept (drafter's choice)

svg.text: ADR-0028 fixes a horizon for F1 to F6 and the corpus none for the rest. Keeping all is "The archetype log remains the maximum
projection" and what replay over "boundary events only" (ADR-0020) needs. ⟨R2⟩ Tolerable only because a fact holds little:
ADR-0070's B5 practice, "Minimize by default".
AS-2 A unit is never kept for less time than its topic.
AS-3 A header outlives its unit: ADR-0004's "hash and a pointer", and a fact.
AS-5 Nothing in class C has a limit; a cut holds no payload but does hold names, an open obligation here as CR-11 is for the
floor.

text.tspan: AS-4 Evidence follows the fact that cites it

svg.text: Attestation evidence is cited by a grant (F1), so kept for the chain's life: the length ADR-0034 left unstated. ⟨R2⟩ ADR-0070 §3's
bill of materials, second-builder evidence and projected provenance, and §4's stand-up declaration, are each on line D-f; the bill
has to be kept for §7.3's advisory-to-revocation test.

text.tspan: AS-6, AS-7 ⟨R2⟩ A production lifetime ends at a fact; a return restarts one

svg.text: ADR-0021 §7 does not say what ends a lifetime; ADR-0070 §3 (e) gives every artifact "A declared end" (expiry, revocation or
retirement), each an entry. The lifetime ends at the last such entry *(drafter's choice)*; without ADR-0070, at the entry the
declaration names, and a B-b line that names none has no at most.
"return is a promotion" (ADR-0070 §6.7): the round's line is again inside its at least. If the unit was disposed of in between,
ADR-0021 §7 cannot be met; the header reads disposed and voters can read that (ADR-0076 §7 RD-4). A gate on such a return
is not decided (Annex B, item 7).

text.tspan: §3 Erasure in the archive · §4 Every absence is explained · §5 Disposition · §6 A closed chain · §7 Holds
§3 Erasure: restated, then how the event reaches the archive

svg.text: Restated. Erasure "is an event — consensus-ordered, modeled in TLA+, recorded in the log it modifies" (ADR-0006), a quorum decision on an anchor-issued roster (ADR-0013
§1), by deletion of sealed topics and plaintext-store entries, crypto-shredding rejected (ADR-0028), the unit "dropped whole" (ADR-0003 A3).
ER-1 The archive erases on the F6 fact and on nothing else; no operator, administrator or program has another path, because "deletion cannot be an out-of-band operator
action" (ADR-0006).
ER-2 Ordered, then complete, and the difference is visible: the erased mark is ordered when every copy is gone; between them the erasure is a listable state. The mark records

text.tspan: the archive's report and proves nothing more.

svg.text: ER-3 Deletion is the mechanism; a destroyed key is at most an addition and never the evidence: ciphertext with no key is "a hole no auditor can distinguish from suppression"
ER-4 No copy exists that an erasure cannot reach: no backup of the governed store unless encrypted under the units' keys and declared (D-0075-3).
ER-5 Nothing derived from a unit's payload lives outside the unit: an index, extract, embedding or summary is inside the container or dropped with it (ADR-0019's shadow;
ADR-0038 finding 3). ⟨R2⟩ A trace of admits is facts; a trace that carries bodies is a derivative.
ER-6 What survives: every fact, the F6 entry among them; the header; the digests the log holds (ADR-0042 §3). Demand type 5 is not supported (ADR-0013 §5); "the pointer is
itself a disclosure" (ADR-0004).
ER-7 An erasure of a unit not in the archive completes at once, with a mark saying not captured or disposed.
ER-8 ⟨R2⟩ A drafting session that reads a unit's body is a copy no erasure reaches, and what it drafts is a derivative that lands in the corpus, where nothing is erased. At the
archetype no body of a unit is read into a drafting session (drafter's choice); facts may be, under ADR-0070 §5.1's mark (D-0075-4 for a provider that deletes verifiably).

text.tspan: §4 Every absence is explained: ADR-0006's required property, at the archive

svg.text: AB-1 For every header exactly one holds: the container is in the governed store; an erased mark cites an F6 entry; a disposed mark cites the schedule line; or the header says
not captured. A header with none of the four is a finding: a loss or a suppression, and the archive cannot tell which.
AB-2 A fact is never lawfully absent: an absent entry under a mark is always a finding. NC-2 (ADR-0013 §4) held at the archive, over every class of ADR-0028 §1.
AB-3 Nothing is dropped before its fact; a drop with no entry before it is a finding against the archive.
AB-4 An erasure rewrites nothing: the Merkle tree is over facts and no payload is a leaf, which is how "recorded in the log it modifies" and "never edited" both hold.
AB-5 Replay survives erasure: conformance replays admits (ADR-0005 §4). What replay loses with a unit is its denials (ADR-0074 §2 H-4).

text.tspan: §5 Disposition at the end of a period

svg.text: DP-1 A unit whose at most has ended is dropped whole, under ER-4 and ER-5. DP-2 Recorded: a disposed mark naming the unit and the line. DP-3 By the schedule in force,
never by a person's choice. DP-5 Only B and D-r are ever disposed of.
DP-4 A clock that fails must fail towards keeping (drafter's choice): disposition waits for the entry that says the period ended, and a replica's own clock disposes of nothing. ⟨R2⟩
ADR-0032 §2's rule turned round: an at most is read as elapsed late, which neither ADR-0032 nor ADR-0070 states; ADR-0070's B9 leaves its clock cell empty, and this belongs
in it. No trusted clock exists (ADR-0045 §6), so an at most in calendar time is a limit a deployment can overrun, not a guarantee of deletion by a date; which clock proposes
the entry is open.

text.tspan: §6 A closed chain: so that the archive is not why the record lapses

svg.text: ADR-0028's open obligation: "The horizon does not survive re-genesis"; "Re-genesis (A-0025) starts a new chain, not a continuation" (ADR-0027). The migration rule is
ADR-0025's to write.
RG-1 Everything is keyed by chain; a successor never writes under a predecessor's id.
RG-2 A closed chain's holdings are kept (drafter's choice): each at least runs as if the chain had continued, down the line of succession; a chain with no successor is kept until a
person with the authority to decide says otherwise, whom no record names.
RG-3 Who reads a closed chain is not decided here: until ADR-0025's rule, the audit authority its own chain declared, and no one under the successor's authority.
RG-4 A closed chain has no log to order an erasure in; until the rule exists its units end by period only. This is a real gap: an erasure duty does not lapse because an
anchor was lost.

text.tspan: §7 Holds: the corpus has none, and good practice requires one

svg.text: HD-1 Names units, or a class and a range, and suspends disposition by period. HD-2 May only preserve: ends nothing, shortens nothing, gives nobody a reading.
HD-3 Also refuses erasure, as policy: a deny on the erasure envelope in a promoted bundle, since "Bundles may only narrow erasure further" (ADR-0028 §2). ⟨R2⟩ Lifting is a
promotion. Placing should not have to wait for a quorum (drafter's recommendation): on ADR-0070 §1's orientation a hold subtracts, and ADR-0050 §4 makes the same
split, "adds need a lease and a peer, denies need neither". No variant of ADR-0050's alphabet places one; until it gains one (Annex B, item 8) a hold is placed by promotion, and
an erasure or a disposition can complete while that promotion is voted. One operator could delay an owed erasure: attribution, not prevention (HD-4).
HD-4 On the record, not secret from the audit authority. HD-5 A regulator's duty to keep is a line's at least, not a hold.

text.tspan: §8 Practice this schedule can express (informative; named from the drafter's knowledge, none read, no compliance claimed) · §9 Degeneracy, and no row added
Keep records of who did what for a fixed term (for example, HIPAA's six years for required documentation)

svg.text: At least on A-F, A-o and E (SC-3)

text.tspan: Limit how long personal data is kept (for example, GDPR's storage limitation)

svg.text: At most on B-r and B-b (§5)

text.tspan: Erase a person's data on request (GDPR's erasure)

svg.text: §3, on the round units that hold it. Not on facts. What F1 to F6 hold of a person is kept, and the basis for that is the deployment's
to state (SC-4)

text.tspan: Account for disclosures (HIPAA's accounting of disclosures)

svg.text: The journal's read entries (ADR-0076 §7), kept as class E

text.tspan: Preserve material for a dispute or an inquiry
Keep certain records on storage that cannot be rewritten (for example, the SEC's broker-dealer rule)

svg.text: The locked store (ADR-0076 §2), for A, C, D and E

text.tspan: Show that a record is authentic, reliable, intact and usable (ISO 15489's four characteristics)

svg.text: K-1's source positions (ADR-0074 §1); the roots and fixity audit (ADR-0076 §5); the read interfaces (ADR-0076 §7)

No row is added by this record. The executor that drops a unit acts inside the governed store's row (ADR-0076 §9), a hold is a deny carried today in a promoted bundle (HD-3), and the schedule is part of the declaration.

text.tspan: §8a The retention boundary in ADR-0070's terms ⟨R2⟩ ⟨K13⟩: B9 made six crossings (drafter's choice; the ids are placeholders, numbering is ADR-0070's), whole

text.tspan: RB-1 Four instants only on paper, two that do not do the job

svg.text: B9-b's and B9-f's instants are accepted records' and nothing implements them: no roster, erasure not built (G11). B9-a's and
B9-c's are Proposed. B9-e has no instant, and B9-d's is too slow to stop what it is for: by ADR-0070 §1, "A boundary with no
instant is not a control. It is a finding", until ADR-0025 and ADR-0050 are amended.

text.tspan: RB-2 The orientation holds on a second axis

svg.text: ADR-0070 §1 orients by "authority, reach or trust"; destroying evidence subtracts none, so read alone it would make erasure
local. ADR-0006 forbids that. The record's own direction is ADR-0028's: towards less record a quorum, an issuance or a
promotion decides; towards more, it is local. B9-b, B9-c, B9-f and lifting a hold go towards less; B9-a and placing a hold
towards more.

text.tspan: RB-3 Disposition is decided when the schedule is promoted

svg.text: No quorum meets to dispose of a unit: the promotion was the decision (SC-4, DP-3), the entry that ends a period carries it out.
ADR-0070 §6.5: "An advance adds nothing the vote did not."

text.tspan: RB-4 Being read is an adversary here too

svg.text: ADR-0070 §1 counts "an adversary to what crosses being read". For B9-b that is the reader who copied before the drop: ER-4
and ER-8 address it, and an export does not (ADR-0076 §8 EX-3).

text.tspan: §10 Ratification condition, item by item (every item Not met, as the record marks it)
State, as the record marks it

At least AbsenceExplained (M_SILENTDROP), FactsSurviveErasure over all six classes (M_ERASEFACT), NoDropBeforeFact (M_EARLYDROP), ErasureReachesEveryCopy (M_STRAYCOPY), NoShadow (M_INDEXEDBODY), HoldOnlyPreserves (M_HOLDDROPS), ClosedChainKept (M_LAPSEATREGENESIS)

Not met. No entry is written

Not met. No amendment is drafted
⟨R2⟩ ADR-0070's row B9 is reconciled with §8a (Annex B, item 7), by an R-revision of that record; if ADR-0070 is withdrawn or narrowed, §8a stands on the accepted records it cites
Not met. ADR-0070 is Proposed on another branch, and nothing in it has changed
⟨R2⟩ The clock that ends an at most is decided (DP-4)

The reference shows an erasure ordered, a unit dropped in every domain and the erased mark; an erasure left incomplete and listed; a disposition at a period's end with its mark; a hold refusing both; a header with no explanation reported as a finding
Not met. Erasure is not implemented, and no roster exists
A deployment declaration carries a schedule under §1, every line filled or marked
Not met. No declaration template exists (ADR-0045, Open obligations)
ADR-0025's migration rule exists, or §6's two gaps are carried on this record's face at ratification
Not met. They are carried: RG-3 and RG-4

text.tspan: A hold as an operator's action, a seventh variant in ADR-0050's alphabet

svg.text: Struck at R2: Not taken *(drafter's choice)*: quicker than a promotion, but it would let one operator and a peer block an erasure a roster had authority to order, and needs a change to a provisional record. ⟨R2⟩ Recommended for placing a hold,
and owed to ADR-0050 (HD-3). On ADR-0070 §1's orientation that is a deny, which the pattern lets an operator make alone and holds them to account for. Lifting stays a promotion

text.tspan: Decide here who reads a closed chain

svg.text: Not taken (RG-3). It is ADR-0025's, and it turns on what a successor anchor may inherit

text.tspan: A closed chain's holdings dropped at re-genesis

svg.text: Rejected (RG-2). "the authority record lapses exactly when it matters most" is ADR-0025's own description of that outcome

text.tspan: A named profile for each regulation

svg.text: Rejected by ADR-0023, restated (§8)
Positive: every kept thing has a line, and the lines the corpus never wrote are marked as the deployment's; the lock and the delete stop contradicting each other; a missing payload reads as erased,

disposed of, never captured, or lost, and the last is a finding; an unfinished erasure is visible; a retention duty and an erasure duty are both expressible; re-genesis no longer ends the record by default;
⟨R2⟩ the boundary is declared in ADR-0070's seven terms and its two weak crossings named.

Negative: everything in the log is kept for the chain's life, the largest possible choice; a person's name in a fact is kept, and no erasure reaches it; ⟨R2⟩ until ADR-0050 gains a deny a hold is as slow

as a promotion and an erasure can beat it; ⟨R2⟩ a drafting session gets what the log says of a round and not what the round said; ⟨R2⟩ an at most is not a deletion date; a closed chain's units cannot be
erased until ADR-0025 says who may; no offline backup of payload; disposition waits on the log; the schedule has lines no one can fill from the corpus.
The migration rule (ADR-0025), for RG-3 and RG-4.
Personal data in facts, headers and cuts (CR-11; ADR-0056's open question): whether a name could be replaced by a reference an erasure can sever is not asked here.
Who may ask for an erasure, and what the roster is shown: no record names the requester.
What the disposed and erased marks cost the log, at one entry per unit.
⟨R2⟩ The operator's deny that places a hold (Annex B, item 8). ⟨R2⟩ The clock that ends an at most. ⟨R2⟩ A gate on a return to an artifact whose unit is gone (AS-7). ⟨R2⟩ A provider's deletion a
deployment can verify (ER-8). ⟨R2⟩ Tenancy: ADR-0070's B24 has no owner and the archive has nothing per tenant.
F1's volume in the cost model, which AS-1 enlarges. The purge interval of the governed store. The findings of Annex A, each another record's to correct.
Narrative: ToO §4.3, §4.4 and the glossary owe schedule, disposition, hold and closed chain if ratified.

4. ADR-0028's bootstrap note says erasure is disabled "until this record and ADR-0013 are ratified", and two paragraphs on that "Ratifying them does not by itself enable erasure".
5. ADR-0003's History row A3 still reads Pending in its State column, with B17 ratifying it below.

text.tspan: ⟨R2⟩ Findings against ADR-0070, from reading it for R2; reported and not changed; ADR-0070 owns each

svg.text: 7. Its B9 row reads "In force". No erasure roster exists, erasure is not implemented, and there is no archive (G9, G11). Its B1 row has the form that fits: "In force as specification".

8. B9 has one instant, the seal. Erasure, disposition and a chain's close are crossings of the same boundary; its Consequences name seven boundaries with no instant and B9 is not among them, though B9-e has none.
9. Its §1 orientation and §9's "Subtraction needs no quorum" are written of authority; neither says that destroying evidence is not that kind of subtraction (RB-2).
10. Its §5.1 has a session read "an intake object, a trace or a Report" and mark its drafts; a Report's content is payload, and the mark does nothing for an erasure (ER-8). Against B20, B22, B29.
11. Its §8 lets recorded traces into the specification graph as evidence without saying they are traces of facts (ER-5). Against B22.
12. Its §6.7 makes a return a promotion without asking whether the returned artifact's Build round is still held (AS-7). Against B1.
13. Its §2.3 gives B9 no clock; a retention period's failure direction is the opposite of ADR-0032 §2's for an interval that subtracts authority (DP-4).

text.tspan: ADR-0076 · The archive is two stores and an index; the log orders the root of every segment; nothing that decides reads the archive without a proof; every reading is by a declared authority and is itself kept
Proposed · C2, C4 · R1 · drafted 2026.11.16, not reviewed

svg.text: Context. One row of the trusted base asks one store to do two opposite things: T-0045-7's identity is "object lock or equivalent" and ADR-0004's store is "built for deletion"; on the common object-store interface a bucket with Object Lock must keep versions, and versions keep what a delete removed. The corpus has asked for integrity without saying of what: ADR-0015's audit chain ends "at a named axiom", ADR-0003 recalls a Merkle root over round envelopes that never reached the record, ADR-0006 wants lawful erasure told apart from

rewriting. The archive must not become an authority by being read: ADR-0035's lineage and ADR-0069's IG-4 (both Proposed) read log positions that a compacted log leaves in the archive. No record says who reads the archive or how: ADR-0028 §3's audit authority is "the anchor plus a declared external auditor role", and the role is open. Status note: C2 (§6's confinement claim is what keeps T-0045-7 delegated), C4 (§11's modules would be the first theorems to cite T-0045-7); C1 is ADR-0075's; C3: Annex B's split of T-0045-7

changes no class. No product named in §2 to §4 has been run. Deployment position: Archetype for §1, §5 to §8 and the requirements of §2 to §4; the products are the reference's choices, substitutable as ADR-0072 §6 says.

text.tspan: §1 Two stores and an index, the table whole · §5 Integrity · §6 Nothing that decides reads the archive without a proof

svg.text: A facts, as segments; C the corpus; D evidence; E the journal
Keep, unchanged, for each line's at least (ADR-0075 §2)
Evidence lost or damaged
B round units
Keep until erasure or period, and then no longer
A unit lost early. A unit not deleted
A projection of both: fields of facts, unit headers, cut manifests
Answer queries
Unavailable, or wrong and caught by a proof (§7 RD-7)

P-1 The two stores share nothing: no bucket, volume, credential or administrator's role. The feeder of facts holds no right to delete anywhere; the only right to delete in the governed store is the executor's, on an F6 entry or the end of a period.
P-2 The index is not the record: dropped and rebuilt from the two stores, the rebuild checked against the roots (§5), as ADR-0072 §1 P-2 checks its own.
P-3 Each part's interface is fixed and its product is not: S3 with Object Lock; S3 without it; the DynamoDB interface ⟨K5⟩.

text.tspan: §6 AR-1 to AR-4: the delegated row's test, as a property

svg.text: AR-1 The admit path does not read the archive: true of the reference today, kept true.

AR-2 A gate, a tally or a tool that needs an entry the log no longer holds takes it only with an inclusion proof against a mark in the log; without one the entry is absent and the gate fails. Lineage (ADR-0035 §1) and IG-4 (ADR-0069 §3a), both Proposed, are the first two
readers bound.
AR-3 Absence only subtracts: no rule lets a missing record count as a clean one.
AR-4 Nothing decides on a unit: a unit is evidence for people and for the Observer's successors in review, and "never admits anything" (ADR-0037 §3).

So an archive that fails in any way, lying included, produces no admit, promotion or issuance the mechanism would otherwise refuse: ADR-0045 §2's test for a delegated row, which §11 asks for as a property.
IN-1 A chain's facts form one Merkle tree in log order, in RFC 9162's form (drafter's choice); a leaf is the hash of one entry's bytes; the root after a segment covers every entry so far.
IN-2 The log orders each root: the held mark names range and root, proposed only for a root the replica recomputed. An auditor has the roots from the log, not from the archive.

IN-3 Two proofs, both served: inclusion (this entry is a leaf under this root) and consistency (a later tree extends an earlier one, nothing before changed). ADR-0015's audit chain can be walked from an effect to the genesis issuance without trusting the store.
IN-4 An erasure touches no leaf (ADR-0075 §4 AB-4); a deployment keeping fewer entries (D-0075-1) keeps their leaf hashes, and every proof holds.

IN-5 A unit is checked against the log as far as the log reaches: every emission carries its admit's index and sequence number (ADR-0005 §2) and the round "seals at the final sequence number" (ADR-0042 §5); Build's container against the sealed topic-set digest (ADR-0021
§4). What the log does not reach is a body's bytes where it holds no digest, and the denials.
IN-6 The journal has a tree of its own and each mark carries its root; the mechanism cannot recompute it and does not vouch for it. Ordering it fixes what the archive said and when.

IN-7 Fixity is audited on a declared cycle: every locked object rehashed in every domain; a mismatch repaired from another domain and journalled, one that cannot be is a finding; the same audit reads the governed store for every unit an erased or disposed mark names, and
a container found is a finding. Each audit writes a dated results file, never edited.

IN-8 No key of the archive's is trusted for anything; the roots are the log's. An outside witness or a timestamp authority (RFC 3161) is an addition with a carrier's standing (ADR-0069 §9 C-2): it may refuse and never admits.

reader's set, and never from the audit authority's (ADR-0028 §4)

The audit authority

text.tspan: erasure entry and a forensic-classes entry and none about readers.

svg.text: RD-3 GraphQL and REST, generated from one model, equal, read-only (ADR-0072 §7's A-1 to A-4, A-6, A-7 as written) ⟨K6⟩.
RD-5 Every past state is read as the newest ⟨K10⟩: a superseded revision, an earlier epoch's rules, a closed chain, an old cut, by the same operations.
RD-6 Every read but a read of C is journalled: reader, set, the ask, and a stated purpose nothing checks. This is the accounting ADR-0028 lists as a requirement its floor "does not
express".
RD-7 An answer about a fact carries its inclusion proof and names its mark. RD-8 A read writes nothing but its journal entry. RD-9 How to read the archive is a document, ADR-0071's
Ex-3, whose bindings point at objects in C and D by digest.
EX-1 Any range a reader may read, as one self-describing package: objects, a manifest of SHA-256 digests, the marks, the proofs; a BagIt bag (RFC 8493) (drafter's choice).
EX-2 Verifies with no access to the archive, against a copy of the log's marks obtained separately.
EX-3 A package of units goes only to a reader of B, is a copy ER-4 does not reach, and is journalled as such; what the recipient owes an erasure is the deployment's to bind.
EX-4 A successor chain's audit authority receives a closed chain's facts as a package once ADR-0025's rule says it may (ADR-0075 §6 RG-3).

svg.text: Not taken. IX-1 has every reading a key condition. An auditor who needs more takes an export and queries their own copy
Positive: the lock and the delete each have a store; an auditor can check one entry without reading the whole record or trusting the archive; the archive can lie and nothing is
admitted on its word; a failed delete can be found; who read what is itself on the record; the documentation's design carries over nearly whole; the index's engine is the least
proven part and the least trusted one.
Negative: two object stores, an index, a tree and a read service for a deployment that has not yet run the mechanism; the lock has to be extended for ever and a lapse is silent
until someone looks; three fault domains under two administrations is a cost many will declare away (D-0076-2); a body's bytes are checked only where the log holds a digest
(IN-5); an export of units is a copy no erasure reaches (EX-3); reader sets as promoted policy make changing an auditor as slow as a promotion; every product

Whether replay is a reader: ADR-0003 0003.5 and ADR-0020 do not say which governs; RD-6 records a replay's reads and settles nothing.
The tree's implementation, pinned, and the canonical bytes of a leaf. A sequence number on denials (ADR-0005 §6), without which IN-5 cannot order them.
The purge interval (GS-3) and the fault-domain numbers (LS-3, GS-5): the deployment writes these. Running the products of §2 to §4, and a second product behind each
interface. Row T-0045-40, if the custodian takes Annex B.

no credential; a Merkle tree whose roots the log orders; nothing that decides reads without a proof; reading by promoted reader sets through GraphQL and REST; exports verify
offline; T-0045-7 delegated with a second row proposed; five degeneracies.

#51). No decision text changes. Not reviewed.

"Define the external auditor role": §7 RD-1 uses the role and does not define it. The entry records the dependence and closes nothing
§5 IN-3 gives the audit chain a means of being walked, and changes no clause

text.tspan: ADR-0035 and ADR-0069 (both Proposed). R-revisions (dependent on ADR-0076,

svg.text: A gate that reads log positions reads them under §6 AR-2 once the log is compacted
The archive mark and its kinds, the journal root in a mark, and the rule on compaction (ADR-0074 §4). When the archive is built, ADR-0033 takes an addendum with the run
The archive's governed store (ADR-0004;
ADR-0074 B)
substrate
Holds a round unit until its erasure or its period's end, and then no
longer
all
delegated
A unit lost early: legibility subtracted. A unit not deleted: an erasure or a limit not
honoured
The deployment declaration, with no lock and no
versioning
A unit that outlives its erasure harms the person it concerns and changes no authority. The mechanism records the archive's report that it is gone and cannot check it

Proposed, not in ADR-0045. T-0045-37 is the last row in force (ADR-0053, Batch 36); T-0045-38 and T-0045-39 are ADR-0056's proposed rows (C10), so T-0045-40 is the next id after them. The row exists only in ADR-0076 Annex B until ADR-0045 takes its amendment; the diagram shows it as the record writes it.
